content.thinking: In the current SCOPe 2.08 release, PA1492 and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase share the same superfamily (c.23.14) but sit in different families, whereas in SCOP 1.69 (from memory, unverified) they were only linked at the fold level—so the relationship was upgraded but doesn't establish shared function. I can't confirm the 1.69 details with my tools since they only query the current release.

answers.answer: In the current release (SCOPe 2.08), PA1492 (PDB 1t1j; d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (PDB 1f8y; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_) are in the same superfamily but different families. Both are class c (alpha/beta), fold c.23 Flavodoxin-like, superfamily c.23.14 N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like. PA1492 is family c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (Pseudomonas aeruginosa). 1f8y is family c.23.14.1 N-deoxyribosyltransferase (Lactobacillus leichmannii). The lowest shared node is therefore the superfamily, which SCOPe treats as probable common ancestry, with the two proteins in separate families (not close sequence or functional relatives). In SCOP 1.69, as I recall the Andreeva et al. 2008 example, PA1492 was not in this superfamily. It had only a fold-level (flavodoxin-like) similarity to the nucleoside deoxyribosyltransferases, which means a shared fold without asserted homology. So the relationship changed from 'similar fold only' to 'same superfamily, different family'. I could not verify the 1.69 placement with the tools because they only query the current release. Limits: superfamily placement supports probable common ancestry but does not show that PA1492 has nucleoside deoxyribosyltransferase activity. SCOPe annotates it only as a hypothetical protein / structural genomics target, so function should not be transferred from 1f8y. A shared fold alone would not be homology evidence.
evidence_used: pretrained knowledge of Andreeva et al. 2008 (SCOP 1.69 placement, not verified by tool)
